title: Layout — centered document, wider default, sidebar variants

meta.subtitle: User wants wider default + a centered-document feel. Five layout options visualised so the right one can be picked.
meta.summary: Five candidate layouts for the kit's wide-screen + centered-document brief. Each shows wide and narrow viewport mockups, where the sidebar toggle lives, and the trade-offs. Decide one; the others are reject-with-reason.

blocks.summary: Today's narrow column on a wide screen looks cramped. User compared a hand-authored HTML page (MEETING-2026-05-22.html in the lakelab task) and judged the wider, centered layout strictly better. Five candidates here — every layout pushes prose to a wider centered column. The variants differ in how the sidebar lives: in-flow column, edge rail, floating drawer, or hybrid.
bullets: Default content width should grow — narrow 860 → 1080, wide 1100 → 1320, with centered alignment.
Centered ‘main’ replaces left-aligned ‘main’ — visually balanced regardless of sidebar state.
Sidebar must remain reachable; five candidate behaviours below.
Pick one; I'll implement the layout + numeric assertions + tests.

blocks.title: Today
blocks.lead: For reference, the current shape — left sidebar in flow, narrow content cell, left-aligned main.

blocks.title: What's wrong
blocks.content: On a 1440-1920 monitor, the 860px content column starts 24px to the right of the sidebar and ends ~720-1000px away from the right viewport edge. Eye scans an off-centre rectangle with a lot of dead space to one side. ‘More cards per row’ in wide mode partially helps but everything is still left-anchored.

blocks.title: Five layout candidates
blocks.lead: Each candidate is a complete layout. Pick the one whose trade-offs match how you actually use the kit.

blocks.title: A — In-flow sidebar, wider centered main

cards.title: Pros
items: Lowest-friction migration — sidebar already exists in flow.
Main column grows AND centers in the remaining grid cell.
Sidebar always visible on wide; collapse to 24px rail still works.
Numeric: main.boundingBox.x = (viewport.width - sidebar.width - main.width) / 2 + sidebar.width.

cards.title: Cons
items: ‘Centered’ is only centered in the cell-after-sidebar — slightly biased right of geometric center.
On a 1920 viewport with 280 sidebar + 1320 main, there's still ~320 px of right margin (the centering uses it half-and-half).
Sidebar collapse changes the centering origin — content shifts when toggled.

blocks.title: Toggle behaviour
blocks.content: Right-edge handle on sidebar (today's). Resize-drag widens / collapses the sidebar; main re-centers around the new available cell. Toggle lives on the sidebar edge — proximity to what it controls.

cards.title: Pros
items: Main is TRULY viewport-centered — geometric center.
Two 24-px rails at the edges keep both nav AND a secondary surface (TOC? notes?) discoverable.
Click rail → drawer slides over main — no reflow disrupts reading.
Mobile is identical: rail + drawer scales down.

cards.title: Cons
items: Popout overlay covers the main column when open — reader must close drawer to keep reading.
Two rails consume 48 px regardless of viewport — wastes width on narrow screens (rails could be edge-only at < 1024).
More mechanism than (A) — slide animation, focus trap, backdrop.

blocks.title: Toggle behaviour
blocks.content: Left rail = nav. Click the rail → popout drawer (page-nav). Right rail = optional secondary surface (page-toc or a future right-rail). Esc / click backdrop / click rail again closes.

blocks.title: C — Floating sidebar, full-bleed when collapsed

cards.title: Pros
items: Default state: main is geometric-centered in the full viewport. Maximum reading space.
Same mechanism on wide AND narrow — one mental model.
Sidebar is hidden by default — reader sees content first, navigation second.
Toggle button is the only persistent chrome left in the top corner.

cards.title: Cons
items: Site-tree visibility cost: reader has to open the drawer to browse pages — friction for first-time visitors.
Sidebar reflows main when open (or covers it as overlay) — pick one; either way there's a layout jolt.
Sticky hamburger is the ONLY navigation cue on first paint; might miss it.

blocks.title: Toggle behaviour
blocks.content: Hamburger in the top-left chrome cluster (current drawer-toggle, promoted to default on all viewports). Click opens a 280-px overlay (or pushes main right). Esc / backdrop / second-click closes.

blocks.title: D — Centered main, sidebar as collapsed icon rail (always visible)

cards.title: Pros
items: Navigation is ALWAYS visible — 48 px icon rail signals the structure on first paint.
Reader can switch pages with one click without opening anything.
Main is centered in (viewport - 48 px) — close to geometric center.
Pattern works the same on narrow viewports (rail becomes a bottom bar).

cards.title: Cons
items: Each top-level page needs a recognisable icon — author maintenance cost.
Rail-expansion DOES shift main horizontally → some readers find this distracting.
More chrome to maintain (icons + labels + hover behaviour).
Doesn't make sense if total page count is small (icons read as decoration).

blocks.title: Toggle behaviour
blocks.content: Hover any rail icon → tooltip with page label. Click → expand rail to 280 px (or navigate directly, depending on second-click semantic). Click outside → re-collapse. Always-visible affordance + first-paint discoverability.

blocks.title: E — Static centered, sidebar lives at top (above content)

cards.title: Pros
items: Strongest centered-document feel — no sidebar to compete for attention.
Main is geometric-centered in the FULL viewport.
Nav is structural (HTML doc convention) but compact.
Same shape on narrow + wide → simplest mental model.

cards.title: Cons
items: Horizontal nav doesn't scale past ~7 top-level pages without scrolling/overflow.
Site-tree hierarchy (plans/wide-screen / plans/naming) needs dropdowns or breadcrumbs.
Loses ‘scroll-spy in sidebar’ — on-page TOC needs its own affordance (right-side mini, or auto-numbered headings).
Largest deviation from today's layout — most code to rewrite.

blocks.title: Toggle behaviour
blocks.content: Top horizontal nav. Click any item → navigate. Dropdowns for nested pages. The on-page TOC (current page outline) lives as a separate small right rail OR a sticky breadcrumb under the top nav.

blocks.title: Decision axes — what to weigh
blocks.lead: Three orthogonal questions resolve the choice.

rows: Is the site-tree always-visible navigation important to you?
Should the content be EXACTLY viewport-centered (geometric)?

blocks.title: Recommendation
blocks.lead: Two strong candidates; pick on the trade between ‘always-visible nav’ vs ‘maximum content focus’.

cards.title: Pick A if
items: You currently rely on the site-tree to navigate.
Slight off-centring of main is acceptable.
You want the smallest code change.

cards.title: Pick D if
items: You want both always-visible nav AND geometric centering.
You're willing to author one icon per top-level page.
The rail-expand shift is acceptable.

cards.title: Pick B if
items: Two surfaces (nav + secondary) are useful enough to keep rails always-on.
Popout-over-content is acceptable.
You want symmetry (rails both sides).

cards.title: Pick C if
items: Reading focus > navigation discoverability.
You usually arrive by URL or search, not browse.
First-paint speed matters (least chrome painted).

cards.title: Avoid E unless
items: You're sure the top-level page count stays small.
Nested-page navigation can be solved by dropdowns / breadcrumbs.
You're OK rewriting the most CSS.

blocks.title: My pick
blocks.content: A — incremental change from today, biggest perceived win for least mechanism. Bump narrow → 1080, wide → 1320, change main alignment from left to center. The sidebar stays in flow on wide viewports and remains a drawer on narrow. If after living with it for a week you still want geometric-center, D is the natural follow-up.

blocks.title: After you pick
blocks.lead: What I'll do once the choice is made.

items: Change `body[data-content-width=narrow/wide/max]` token values to the new defaults.
Change `main { margin: 0 auto }` so main is centered in its grid cell (today it's left-aligned in some cases).
Update the 3-segment width-toggle icon's labels (narrow/wide/max → ‘compact / default / wide’ if labels change).
Add a numeric assertion test: `main.boundingBox.x` close to expected center within ±2 px on a fixed-width viewport.
Update the wide-screen.json plan with the chosen layout's CSS + commit notes.
